narrative: Markets are grappling with a tech-led correction triggered by rising skepticism around AI capital expenditure monetization ahead of mega-cap earnings. Compounding equity pressure, Fed Chair Warsh signaled a potential December rate hike, warning that financial conditions are not yet tight enough. Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East has heavily disrupted energy transit, with Strait of Hormuz vessel traffic plunging and Brent crude sustaining levels above $113/bbl on threats to Iranian infrastructure. Simultaneously, traders are bracing for volatility around the US midterm elections and the US Treasury quarterly refunding announcement. While mega-cap tech faces sustained headwinds, select strategists argue the post-midterm environment could serve as a clearing mechanism to buy broader equity dips.

Nasdaq.why: The index has entered a technical correction, with Paul Dobson of Bloomberg News and Jennifer Lee of BMO Capital Markets citing heavy short positioning and severe market impatience regarding AI capex monetization.

S&P 500.why: Mike Wilson of Morgan Stanley recommends buying the dip regardless of the midterm outcome as a clearing event, though anchors observe cautious sentiment heading into election results and earnings.

Gold.why: Gold was not covered in the provided notes.

Oil.why: Goldman Sachs raised its Brent forecast to $105/bbl, with prices already above $113/bbl as Strait of Hormuz daily vessel transit plunges from 135 to roughly 12 amid military threats.

priced_in: Nasdaq 100 has priced in its third market correction of the year.
RBA 25 bps rate hike to 4.85% is largely baked into expectations.
Potential for a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.
Betting markets and polls pricing in a strong performance for Democrats in the US midterms.
Fatigue and skepticism over hyperscaler AI capex returns following Alphabet and Amazon results.
debates: AI capex sustainability: Foxconn Chairman Young Liu insists AI demand is genuine and outstripping capacity, while tech analysts and BMO emphasize market impatience with spending returns.
Post-midterm equity direction: Mike Wilson of Morgan Stanley sees a buying opportunity regardless of the winner, whereas show anchors note caution ahead of policy outcomes.
Yield trajectory: Lombard Odier argues political gridlock from midterms could curb fiscal deficits and flatten yields, contrasting with Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish stance supporting higher rates.
